The repository's accepted ADR 014 specifies a singleton merge-queue reconciler in the monolith, implemented as a DBOS workflow ticking every 30 seconds with queue concurrency 1 across HPA replicas. ## Evidence - docs/decisions/platform/014-stateless-merge-queue-reconciler.md: Decision - git commit 7cf9c71d2

ADR 014 defines merge order as the age of PRs carrying the ready-to-merge label; dependency ordering is expressed by when the label is applied rather than by separate ordering metadata. ## Evidence - docs/decisions/platform/014-stateless-merge-queue-reconciler.md: Label state machine and One action per tick

When a queued PR has red checks, the reconciler removes ready-to-merge and comments the reason; re-labeling after a fix re-enters the queue. ## Evidence - docs/decisions/platform/014-stateless-merge-queue-reconciler.md: One action per tick

ADR 014 specifies that a dirty rebase always spawns an Ember agent running Sol with a prompt to rebase the PR onto current main; the reconciler does not use a model to judge conflict difficulty. ## Evidence - docs/decisions/platform/014-stateless-merge-queue-reconciler.md: Escalation is deterministic, never a model's judgment call

The merge-queue design treats a Sol-generated resolution commit as unreviewed code: the agent never merges or changes labels, and the PR must pass through the judgment-tier review gate before ready-to-merge is reapplied. ## Evidence - docs/decisions/platform/014-stateless-merge-queue-reconciler.md: Escalation and Security sections
